--- title: "Einführung in R und Quarto" subtitle: "Final Session!
Dynamic Documents with R Markdown" author: "Andreas Haupt" bibliography: IntRo.bib format: revealjs: theme: style.scss css: global.css slideNumber: true fig-align: center editor: source execute: echo: false message: false warning: false --- ## Work flow ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} The normal work flow: 1. R script which contains the *R code* that produces, 2. Our R output: *Figures and Tables*, 3. An MS Word document, which is the *report* describing our results. ![](images/Folder.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} . . . **It's disadvantages:** 1. Every time the output changes, we have to revise the Word document. 2. If we comment our R code a lot (as is good practice), we have excessive `#`, and much will be repeated in the 'Data and Methods' section of the Word document. $\rightarrow$ R Markdown combines R and Markdown to overcome these limitations. ::: ::: --- ## {background-image="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Markdown-mark.svg/640px-Markdown-mark.svg.png"} ## MS Word versus Markdown ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} Word is a so-called 'What You See is What You Get' text editor. That is, you edit your text and it looks just like the final *formatted document*. ![](images/MSWord.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} . . . Markdown separates text editing in *source files*, from the resulting *formatted output*. The source files contain your text and very simple formatting commands: ```markdown # This is a (level 1) header This is just some plain text, maybe an introduction to your final paper. ## This is a (level 2) sub-header Again this is just some simple text. But in this text, I also want to *emphasize* something. In fact, I want to make it **bold**! ``` ![](images/MarkdownExample1.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: --- ## {background-image="https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/images/hex-rmarkdown.png"} ## R Markdown ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} R Markdown allows you to insert *R code chunks* into your Markdown source file: ````markdown # This is a (level 1) header This is just some plain text, maybe an introduction to your final paper. ## This is a (level 2) sub-header Again this is just some simple text. But in this text, I also want to *emphasize* something. In fact, I want to make it **bold**! And this is some R code: ```r mean(c(1, 2, 3, NA), na.rm = TRUE) ``` ```` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} . . . When you turn the source file into a formatted output, the R code will be *evaluated* and with its output, nicely rendered and inserted into your formatted document: ![](images/MarkdownExample2b.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Getting started with R Markdown ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} First, open your R Studio project and install 'rmarkdown'. ```r install.packages("rmarkdown") ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} . . . ::: {.centered} Then start a new R Markdown document. ::: ![](images/RMarkdown1.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Getting started with R Markdown ![](images/RMarkdown2.png){width="50%"} ## Getting started with R Markdown ![](images/RMarkdown3.png){width="80%"} --- ## Klick 'Knit' to compile ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](https://ih0.redbubble.net/image.543341178.1637/flat,750x,075,f-pad,750x1000,f8f8f8.u1.jpg){width="100%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/RMarkdown4.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## What happens in the background ![](https://d33wubrfki0l68.cloudfront.net/61d189fd9cdf955058415d3e1b28dd60e1bd7c9b/9791d/images/rmarkdownflow.png){width="60%"} ## Four remaining topics 1. Markdown formatting commands, 2. R Code chunk options, 3. The YAML header (e.g., how to produce a word file), 4. Citation. ## Markdown formatting commands ![](images/MarkdownCommands.png){width="100%"} ## Exercise 1 (20 Minutes) Revise your R Markdown template to a draft of your final paper: 1. Delete the template text. 2. Add a brief intro about the topic of your final paper (see Exam) to the R Markdown document. 3. Give that paragraph the heading "Introduction". 4. Use Markdown code to emphasize what your outcome is. 5. Make a list of some of the the predictor variables you consider to investigate. 6. Mention that you will analyze the ESS and embed a link to the project homepage. 7. Knit it. ## R code chunks ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} You can initiate an R code chunk with $\rightarrow$ Everything between ` ```{r} ` ... ` ``` ` is evaluated as R code. Moreover, results produced by that R code are pasted into your document. R output can be customized with [chunk options](http://yihui.name/knitr/options/), which you can add to the initiation: ` ```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE} ` - `include = FALSE` prevents code and results from appearing in the final document, although R will evaluate the code. - `echo = FALSE` prevents code, but not the results from appearing in the finished file. - `message = FALSE` prevents messages that are generated by code from appearing in the final document. - `warning = FALSE` prevents warnings that are generated by code from appearing in the final document. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ````markdown ```r ``` P.S.: You should write {r}, not r ```` ````markdown ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 13 ``` ::: ::: P.S.: You should write {r}, not r ```` ::: ::: ## Further important R code chunks ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} #### Options for (regression) tables as output: - `results = 'asis'` prevents Knitr from further processing the R output. This is necessary, for instance, when you generate an html regression table with 'texreg'. Note that this will not work with a Word document as output. ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} #### Options for figures as output: - `out.width = "90%"` size of the figure in % of the width of your document. - `fig.align = "center"` centers the figure in the middle of the document. Alternatives are `"left"` or `"right"`. - `fig.cap = "This is my beautiful figure"` adds a caption to the figure. - `dpi = 200` defines pixel resolution of the figure. - `fig.width = 8` defines the width of the figure in inches. - `fig.height = 4` defines the height of the figure in inches. ::: ::: ## Exercise 2 (15 Minutes) Add three R code chunks to your final paper: 1. Add a code chunk that loads the libraries that you are going to use. Make sure that R evaluates the chunk, but that it gives no warnings, no messages, etc.. 2. Add a chunk that downloads the ESS data pipes it into a `transmute()` and performs some initial recodings. 3. Add a code chunk that adds a figure (histogram or scatter plot) to your final document. ## The YAML header (Meta data for your document) ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ```yaml title: My Title subtitle: My subtitle author: Merlin Schaeffer date: "2026-09-24" output: html_document ``` ![](images/rmarkdownoutputformats.png){width="70%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Among others, the following additional output formats are available: - `pdf_document` creates a PDF via LaTeX, which you will need to install. RStudio will prompt you if you don’t already have it. - `word_document` for Microsoft Word documents (.docx). - `odt_document` for Open Document Text (.odt). - `rtf_document` for Rich Text Format (.rtf). ::: ::: ## The YAML header (Meta data for your document) ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ```yaml title: My Title subtitle: My subtitle author: Merlin Schaeffer date: "2026-09-24" output: ioslides_presentation ``` ![](images/rmarkdownoutputformats.png){width="70%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} You might even try out Presentations: - `ioslides_presentation` makes HTML presentation with ioslides. - `slidy_presentation` makes HTML presentation with W3C Slidy. - `beamer_presentation` makes a PDF presentation with LaTeX Beamer (if you have installed Latex). - `powerpoint_presentation` makes an MS PowerPoint presentation. `---` defines the beginning of a new slide. ::: {.note} I personally use [Xaringan](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/xaringan.html) to make these slides. ::: ::: ::: ## Citation ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} If you do not work with any software to manage your literature yet, start using (open source) [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/)! ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45201036/52821337-90ef4f00-30bf-11e9-9087-01734395656a.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/Bibtex1.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Citation (Export your references as 'Bibtex' file) ![](images/Bibtex2.png){width="40%"} ## Citation (Export your references as 'Bibtex' file) ![](images/Bibtex3.png){width="70%"} ## Citation (Export your references as 'Bibtex' file) ![](images/Bibtex4.png){width="50%"} ## Citation (Export your references as 'Bibtex' file) ![](images/Bibtex5.png){width="75%"} ## In-text citation and list of references ::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} Add Bibtex file as bibliography to your YAML header: ```yaml title: My Title subtitle: My subtitle author: Merlin Schaeffer date: "2026-09-24" output: html_document bibliography: IntRo.bib ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} . . . Simple in-text citation in R Markdown: ```markdown This is a claim for which I need a reference [@wilkinsonReligiosityAuthoritarianismHomophobia2004]. I continue with my paper. ... To finally add the list of reference, I simply add: # References ``` ![](images/Bibtex6.png){width="100%"} ::: ::: ## Literatur ::: {#refs} ::: ## {background-image="https://mareds.github.io/r_course/img_site/Tidyverse_packages.png"} . . .
**Thank you for a fun course!**

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
